scope: Research/proposal only: shareable Rust core for Kedra builds and declarative OS configuration. No implementation, migration, benchmarks or runtime qualification.

claims.claim: Shared source still needs platform-specific toolchain, loader, packaging and distribution adapters; historical Evopedia deployment demonstrates concrete portability friction.
Replacing dependency inputs while retaining prior immutable artifacts differs from mutating an installed store object and preserves rollback choices.
The author explicitly leaves cross-compilation investigation incomplete; 2011 platform experiments do not establish current support or current Nixpkgs platform semantics.

claims.claim: Declarative machines/networks plus an imperative driver instantiate real services and required topology; tests and environments become build artifacts.
Shared immutable software and per-VM mutable storage reduce environment duplication; isolated control sockets avoid fixed-port conflicts.
NixOS guest, noninteractive-tool and single-host small-network limits qualify generality; historical five-run timings are not present-day Kedra benchmarks.

claims.claim: Functions describe package/test variants and their environment; platform-specific execution consumes the declared dependencies.
Building with Nix paths/tools does not prove native distribution builds; separate generated VM builds cover native RPM/Debian environments.
Automatic configuration-space exploration and failure isolation are future work, not demonstrated scheduler capabilities.

claims.claim: Language evaluation describes a graph of imperative build actions; it is a separate operation from executing those actions.

Maximal sharing plus evaluation memoization reuses equal closed terms, but substitution needs closed-term optimization; non-strict arguments and low-sharing programs qualify performance and memory claims.
Simplified error treatment and historical evaluator benchmarks do not define current Nix compatibility or predict Rust performance.
